answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. It survives because finality only counts for established attestators, so a fresh cluster cannot push transactions until it proves honesty across many epochs. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a violet as the anchor of the cost.
